what: EcoShift /api/liveconditions run on 16 Nov 2026 after adding NASA fire detections (VIIRS and MODIS through NASA GIBS), NASA POWER MERRA-2 soil wetness and the stricter burn test. Same requests as burn-check-2026-11-16.json.

fire.line: NASA fire satellites (VIIRS/MODIS, via NASA GIBS): fire detected over or within 400 m of Farmland near Patiala on 2026-11-03, 2026-11-05 (2026-11-02 to 2026-11-15). NASA had not yet published the newest maps for VIIRS Suomi NPP (latest 2026-11-02).

soil.line: NASA MERRA-2 model soil wetness (NASA POWER; 0 = dry, 1 = saturated; a model, not SMAP): root zone 0.35, top 5 cm 0.2 on 2026-11-12, against an average of 0.42 (top 0.38) for 10-30 to 11-12 in 2001-2025: close to normal.

warnings.text: Poor air (fine dust PM2.5 94.1 µg/m³, Copernicus CAMS): limit long hard work outdoors.

Burned ground, about 8.4 acres, in the south-east part of Farmland near Patiala, confirmed by fire: NASA MODIS Terra and Aqua saw active fire over this field on 2026-11-03, 2026-11-05 (NASA GIBS), and between 2026-10-28 and 2026-11-14 Sentinel-2 saw the burn ratio drop sharply and the ground turn dark like charred residue. Burning crop residue sends most of its nitrogen and sulfur into the air and burns off organic matter, so the soil there is less fertile and bare to wind and water erosion. If it was burned: plan extra nitrogen, test the soil, and next time leave or work in the residue.

Farmland near Patiala was 98% bare soil on 2026-11-14. Bare soil over winter loses topsoil to wind and water; a cover crop or leaving residue protects it.

Farmland near Patiala: low organic matter (about 9.6 g of carbon per kg of topsoil). Cover crops and leaving residue build it up and help the soil hold water.
